sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of injury sustained by him in Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief facts of the case of petitioner is as under:
That on 23-05-2023 at about 5-40 p.m she was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05/LE-5982 on the left side of 50 feet road, Avalahalli, Bangalore, when she reached near Nayara Petrol bunk, at that time, driver of Ambulance bearing Reg.No.KA-42/G-1041 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to her motor cycle and caused the accident.
As a result of which she sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bangalore wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, treatment,
transportation, nourishment and other incidental charges.

3. It is contended that, prior to accident she was hale and healthy and she was a Tailor by profession and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries she could not able to do her day to day activities as earlier and suffering pain, mental shock and agony and also put to financial hardship.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle and in this regard the Byatarayanapura Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of offending vehicle in Cr.No.191/2023 for the offences punishable u/sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the Insurer of offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest and costs.
4. In response to issuance of notice, respondent no.1 did not appear before the tribunal and hence he was placed exparte.
On the other hand the respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed its written statement.
5. The respondent No.2 in its written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.
While admitting about insurer (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 of Ambulance bearing Reg.No.KA-42/G-1041 restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further this respondent denied the entire case of the petitioner.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner herself, hence the petition is bad of non joinder of necessary parties.
Further denied the age, income and avocation of petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and expenses Lavanya.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:-
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 23.05.2023 at about 05.40 p.m., near Nayara petrol bunk, 50 feet road, Avalahalli, Bengaluru, due to negligent act of driving of the rider of Ambulance bearing registration No.KA42 G1041 as alleged in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?

The petitioner in order to prove the case, Petitioner herself got examined as PW.1 and also examined MRO of Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, as PW.2 and also examined Dr.Ramesh, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital,
Bangalore as PW.3.

They got marked documents as Ex.P1 to 21.
8.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 did not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments on both side.

10. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 11. Issue No.1:- Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and filed affidavit stating that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and she sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In her cross-examination denied the suggestion that at the time of accident she was going on right side of the road.
Further denied the suggestion that when the ambulance was coming at that Lavanya.

Further denied the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 suggestion that, accident was not occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and she sustained injuries in the accident.

12. On perusal of exhibited documents which disclose that, the Ex.P.1 - FIR is registered by Byatarayanapura Traffic Police against driver of offending vehicle in Cr.No.191/2023 for the offences punishable U/sec.279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.2 is the Complaint issued by father of the petitioner to the Sub Inspector of Police,
Byatarayanapura Traffic P.S. stating that, on the date, place and time of accident on 23-05-2023 at about 5-40 p.m. he received call from his daughter i.e., petitioner herein in respect of accident and after the accident, she was shifted to Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain hospital in the offending vehicle for treatment and when he visited the hospital, therein the doctors have advised to the petitioner to undergo operation for her right shoulder and due to taking care of his daughter in the hospital and lodged the complaint on 24-5-2023.
Ex.P3 is the Spot sketch it discloses that near Bengaluru one junction driver of offending vehicle took his vehicle to right side and dashed the petitioner's vehicle and caused the accident.
Ex.P4 is the Spot mahazar.
Ex.P5 is the notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act issued by the Sub Inspector of Police, Byatarayanapura Traffic P.S. to the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
To the said notice the respondent (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 No.1 i.e., owner of offending vehicle has given reply as per Ex.P6.
Ex.P7 is the copy of Wound certificate issued by Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru it discloses that the petitioner has sustained two simple and one grievous injury.

Ex.P10 is the Copy of discharge summary issued by Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru it discloses that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 23-05-2023 to 26-05-2023 and she has sustained fracture medial 3rd of right clavicle, for which Open reduction internal fixation done under general anesthesia on 24-05-2023.
13. The counsel for respondent argued that this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, hence the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, the petitioner is also contributed to the accident.
But, to prove its contention the respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on its behalf.
14. On perusal of Ex.P8 - copy of IMV report it discloses that the both vehicles are involved in the accident.

It also discloses the damages caused to the offending vehicle are as under:
1. Front right side bumper, fender, indicator and rear view mirror damaged.

Further, damages caused to the petitioner's vehicle are as under:

It is opined that the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of motor vehicles.

Ex.P9 is the copy of Charge sheet it shows that after completion of investigation, the Investigation Officer of Byatarayanapura Traffic Police has filed Charge sheet against driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.

The petitioner got examined MRO of Bhagwan Mahaveen Jain hospital as PW.2 and she has produced Authorization letter, MLC,
Police intimation, entire Case sheet and X-ray as per Ex.P15 to 19.
Therefore it clearly goes to show that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Accordingly, I have answered the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

16. Petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident she was hale and healthy and (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 Tailor by and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Due to accidental injuries, she could not able to do her work as earlier, resulting loss of earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
17. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P8 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and medical records and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.

Ex.P7 Wound certificate discloses that the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling and tenderness present over the right clavicle,
2. Abrasion over back of right hand 3. Abrasion over front of right knee
It is opined that, injury No.1 is grievous and injury No.2 and 3 are simple injuries.
Therefore by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and opinion of the doctor, this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

18. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P10 - discharge summary issued by Bhagwan Mahaveer Jain Hospital, Bengaluru it discloses that she (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 took treatment as an inpatient from 23-05-2023 to 26-05-2023 for 4 days and she has sustained fracture medial 3rd of right clavicle, for which Open reduction internal fixation done under general anesthesia on 24-05-2023.

During the said period,
the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet,
transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant Lavanya.M.S vs District Health Officer on 11 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32761446/
5 charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, she is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
19. Medical Expenses:-

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11 for Rs.1,08,598/-.
There is no contradiction to disbelieve the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
The respondent has not denied the said bills produced by the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,08,598/- under this head.
20. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, she has not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
To prove her age, the petitioner has produced her Aadhaar card copy.
As per Ex.P14 copy of Aadhaar card the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 16-12-2002.
Therefore, this tribunal has considers the age of the petitioner as 21 years at the time of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is '18'.
22.

sentences.text: To prove the percentage of disability and injuries sustained by the petitioner, she got examined Doctor as PW.3.
In his chief affidavit doctor has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained:- fracture of medial 1/3rd of right clavicle and internal fixation of clavicle was done.
Further deposed that the radiological examination shows fractures united with implants in situ.
Further assessed the permanent physical disability of 19% to right upper limb and that of to the whole body at 7%.
The PW.3 has produced OPD card and X-ray which are marked as Ex.P20 and 21.
In the cross examination PW.3 admitted that, it is true to suggest that, I have not treated the personally.
With difficulty petitioner can do her day to day activities.
It is true to suggest that fracture is united.

However, by considering the evidence of doctor and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, medical records, this tribunal has taken the disability at 7% to the whole body as assessed by the doctor.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 18 x 7%/100 = Rs.2,41,920/-.
23.
Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.16,000/- per month and she was admitted in the hospital for 4 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of her stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation for atleast two months.
Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 2) under this head.

6 24. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

sentences.text: Since the petitioner has sustained two simple and one grievous injury as per wound certificate and took treatment as an inpatient for 4 days in the hospital.

Therefore by considering the nature of injuries sustained by her and on account of injuries the claimant has to undergo discomfort and unhappiness in her future life, hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Towards future medication:- The PW.3 doctor has stated in his examination in chief affidavit that, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
In the cross examination doctor admitted that, " fractures are united ".
Neither the petitioner nor the doctor have produced estimation for future medication.
However, by considering the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and evidence of doctor, this tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
26. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in Rs. No.
1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 30,000-00 2.
Attendant charges, extra Rs. 30,000-00 nutritious food and conveyance charges 3. Medical Expenses Rs. 1,08,598-00 4. Loss of income during laid Rs. 32,000-00 up period
5. Loss of future income on Rs. 2,41,920-00 account of permanent disability 6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 30,000-00 unhappiness 7.
Towards future medication Rs. 20,000-00 Total Rs. 4,92,518-00 (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3565/2023 27.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,92,518/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
28. Regarding liability:- The respondent no.1 is the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending vehicle.
In the written statement the respondent no.2 admitted about insurer of offending vehicle.
Therefore, respondents No.1 being R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 being Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However,
primary liability is held on respondent no.2 who is insurer of the offending vehicle.
Further respondent no.2 is directed to deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two Lavanya.

Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

29. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,92,518/- (Rupees  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3565/2023  Four lakhs ninety two thousand five hundred and eighteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
After deposit, out of her share amount 70% with interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment directly to her account on proper verification and identification of the documents and the remaining her share amount of 40% with interest shall be kept in FD in her name in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years, with a liberty to withdraw the accrued interest periodically.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
